title: The effect of changing constituents on tensile mechanical properties of HfNbTaTiZr high entropy alloy: A molecular dynamics study.

recollection.starting_material: Bulk equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy modeled as a random solid solution on a body-centered cubic lattice
recollection.intervention: Molecular-dynamics uniaxial tensile tests at room temperature with systematically varied constituent ratios (e.g. ±10 at.% of one element at a time), using an embedded-atom method potential for refractory metals
recollection.structure: Single-phase BCC solid solution with periodic boundary conditions (≈200 000 atoms), occasionally showing nanoscale short-range order when certain element concentrations were elevated
recollection.mechanism: Plasticity controlled by dislocation nucleation and glide, with pinning by local lattice distortions from size-mismatched atoms; higher Hf or Zr content increased lattice distortion and dislocation barrier
recollection.results: Increasing Hf or Zr by 10 at.% raised the simulated 0.2% proof stress from ~4.8 GPa to ~6.1 GPa and ultimate tensile strength from ~7.2 GPa to ~8.5 GPa; reducing Nb or Ta had the opposite effect, lowering yield by ~1.0 GPa. Work hardening rates correlated positively with the degree of local chemical short-range order.

score.note: The recollection correctly identifies MD tensile testing of a BCC random alloy with constituent variation, but it misstates the composition scheme and atom count and invents short-range-order observations. Its dislocation-pinning mechanism is broadly relevant but assigns strengthening to the wrong compositional trends. All reported strength values and trends substantially disagree with the paper.
